pl-l2d42c6-d1e108.summary: Lists, with Gregory, seven capital or principal vices: vainglory, anger, envy, acedia or sadness, avarice, gluttony, and lust, signified, as Chrysostom says, by the seven peoples holding the promised land. claims: All evils arise from seven capital vices.

pl-l2d42c6.summary: Lists the seven capital or principal vices, with Gregory: vainglory, anger, envy, acedia or sadness, avarice, gluttony, and lust, signified, as Chrysostom says, by the seven peoples holding the promised land. From these as from seven springs flow all deadly corruptions of souls; they are called capital because all evils originate from them.
claims: They are vainglory, anger, envy, acedia or sadness, avarice, gluttony, and lust.
The seven peoples of Canaan signify them.
All evils originate from the capital vices.
